title: Julius:
headline: A stranger gets $10. He gives it to a mom, because he just lost his.
story: Nick asks a man in Bryant Park one question: would you help someone you will never meet? Julius says yes, because his mom taught him that caring often means you never see who you help. Nick hands him a $10 Watsi card. He scrolls the patients and stops on the moms. He lost his own mother a week ago. Then Nick asks if he is happy, and he answers honestly: not sure, but grateful for the people around him.

This is Watsi's whole promise in one person: a real human, a direct gift, and you know where your $10 went. It must feel warm and hopeful, never sad. The grief is one honest beat in the middle. The video moves on with him.
do: Open on frame 1 with Nick's question as on-screen text. No fade, no logo.
Keep captions on screen the whole time. One text at a time.
Make the name super bigger than you think. First name only.
Let the grief line sit in silence for 1 second.
Blur every readable gift-card code (card and phone screen).
dont: No sad music, slow motion, black-and-white or "in memory" text.
No title card or logo at 0:00. No text under the logo.
No full-screen brand graphics. Max two brand touches in the whole cut.

decisions.b: Production Planning row 12949181905 still reads Reference = Requested, owner Nick. Sonam suggested givewithjose.com on 15 Sep. A producer has to pick it. Claire does not.
This plan uses a quiet bed with silence at the grief line, so the cut does not feel flat. Who Gives cuts use no music, but Julius is a gift-card cut. Yes or no?

The 30 Sep rule is no somber sadness. The plan keeps “I just recently lost mine” because it is why he picks a mom, and it turns hopeful within 15 seconds. The cut is built so the line can be lifted without a re-edit.
watsi.org (as planned), or the Who Gives card “Tell us your story”? The 6 Oct direction asks for that card on Who Gives street cuts.
The September Spirit folder is named “_2025”. Confirm it is still the current face before titles are burned in.
